nearest_prs.read: Body read: put a CD back in its jewel case, set its 15 mm hole within 1.9 mm of the hub and press it onto the sprung teeth, then shut the lid.
nearest_prs.comparison: Shared: centring a holed disc on a hub then a snap. Theirs lifts a 16 g disc by its edge onto a hub. Ours slides a 300 g, 43 cm pad that cannot be lifted by the gripper across a high-friction grip face to concentric, then presses a separate sprung centre lock 41 mm through its hole until its clip catches; different object, scale, occupation and two-part mechanism.

physical_skill: Slide a 43 cm, 300 g rigid pad lying 5 cm off-centre across a high-friction driver face to within 1 cm of concentric (pushing at its rim, with the other hand or after release), then press a 60 g sprung centre lock 41 mm down against about 6 N through the pad's 9 cm hole until the clip catches, and take both hands at least 3 cm away.
valid_shortcuts: Build-session runs on the final task.py (after 04:43): scripted demo 1.0 in three runs; do-nothing, careless (press the lock on the off-centre pad: the stem lands on the pad and cannot reach home) and other red-team variants scored 0 or 0.25 as the scoring text states. The 7.0 cm stem only passes the 9.0 cm hole within about 1 cm of centre, so the lock cannot be clicked without centring; knocking the pad off the driver zeroes the trial; holding on caps at 0.5. The one-arm route (slide, release, press) is a legitimate solution and is stated in the README.
distinct_from_nearest: No known task in any state involves a floor machine, burnisher, pad driver or centre lock. Nearest live skill is the CD-on-hub (2342), which differs in scale, grasp (lift vs slide), mechanism (hub teeth vs separate sprung centre lock) and occupation. Residual risks: a reviewer may read it as another 'centre then click' task, or question that the driver is level and fixed rather than on a tipped-back machine (stated in fidelity).
